# Introduction:

The CityRideLite project is a console‑based
Java application designed to simulate a simplified public transport fare
system. Its main purpose is to let users manage and track their journeys while
applying rules such as zone‑based pricing, discounts, and daily fare caps. The
program allows users to add, view, search, update, and delete journeys, with
fares calculated automatically based on zones travelled, time band (peak or off‑peak),
and passenger type, including adults, students, children, and senior citizens.
It also keeps track of daily spending and applies the correct cap for each
passenger category. To ensure data persistence, the application supports saving
and loading journeys in JSON format, as well as importing and exporting records
through CSV files. An admin menu with password protection is included for
configuration management. Overall, the system demonstrates solid use of object‑oriented
programming, file handling, input validation, and structured program design.  

# Analysis:

**Analysis of the program specification**

The main requirements
of the system aim to transform the basic fare calculator into a more complete
and realistic transport management application. To accomplish this, the system
must support two user roles-riders and administrators-each with distinct
responsibilities, ensuring that the paragraph maintains a clear, unified focus
as recommended in guidance about keeping one main idea per paragraph. Riders
should be able to create profiles, record their journeys, and monitor daily travel
and spending, while administrators need tools to configure fares, discounts,
daily caps, and peak/off‑peak time settings. The system must also provide full
journey management, including adding, viewing, searching, updating, and
deleting records, with accurate fare calculations based on zones, time bands,
and passenger types, and the correct application of discounts and daily caps.
Maintaining coherence within the paragraph aligns with guidance that readers
rely on early sentences to understand direction and purpose . Additionally,
data persistence is required through JSON saving/loading and CSV import/export
to prevent data loss. Robust input validation and error handling must be
included to maintain reliability, and the system should follow object‑oriented
principles by organising functionality into separate classes, supporting
clarity and structure within the system- similar to how strong paragraphs
maintain organised and relevant development. 

**Input/Output Process Table**

| **Input**                 | **Process**                                   | **Output**                                |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| User menu choice (1–13)   | Display menu and route to selected function   | Appropriate feature executed              |
| Start zone, End zone      | Validate input and calculate zones crossed    | Zones crossed value                       |
| Time band (PEAK/OFF_PEAK) | Convert input to enum and validate            | Accepted or error message                 |
| Passenger type            | Apply discount rate based on type             | Discount amount calculated                |
| Journey details           | Calculate base fare and final fare (with cap) | Charged fare displayed                    |
| Journey object            | Store in list and update daily spending       | “Journey added successfully”              |
| Journey list              | Loop through list to display journeys         | List of journeys shown                    |
| Search zones              | Compare with stored journeys                  | Matching journey displayed or “Not found” |
| Updated journey inputs    | Recalculate fare and update record            | “Journey updated successfully”            |
| Journey index (delete)    | Remove journey and adjust spending            | “Journey deleted”                         |
| Fare inputs               | Calculate fare without saving                 | Fare displayed                            |
| Journey list (JSON save)  | Convert objects to JSON using Gson            | File saved confirmation                   |
| JSON file                 | Read and convert back to objects              | Journeys loaded into system               |
| Journey list (CSV export) | Convert to CSV format and write file          | CSV file created                          |
| CSV file                  | Read and parse into Journey objects           | Journeys imported                         |
| Passenger type spending   | Track and compare with daily cap              | Daily spending summary shown              |
| Admin password            | Authenticate user                             | Access granted or denied                  |

# Evaluation:

**Effectiveness of the program:**

The CityRideLite program successfully meets
its primary requirements by applying all key functionalities expected of the
system. Users can manage journeys efficiently through features that allow
adding, viewing, searching, updating, and deleting records, thereby it fully
meets the main goal of journey management. The fare calculation component
functions as designed, accurately accounting for zones, time bands, and
passenger categories, and applying appropriate discounts while applying the
daily spending cap. This demonstrates that the system processes fares both
reliably and accurately. The program further meets the requirement to ensure
data retention by allowing users to save and load data in JSON format and to
import or export records using CSV files, making it easy to store and reuse
information whenever needed. Input validation, achieved through exception
handling, enhances the program’s stability by reducing the risk of errors or
system crashes caused by invalid user input.Taken together, these features show
that the program not only fulfils all specified requirements but also provides
a durable and dependable user experience.

**If the program meet all the requirements?** **If not, why not?**

The CityRideLite program meets most of the
key requirements set out in the brief and is effective in delivering the core
functionalities of the system. It provides a durable journey and management
features, including adding, viewing, searching, updating, and deleting
journeys, which form the core of the application. The fare calculation logic is
accurately implemented, taking into account zones, time bands, and passenger
types, and correctly applies discounts and daily spending caps to ensure
reliable results. The program also satisfies the data persistence requirement
through JSON save/load and CSV export/import capabilities. The application of
object-oriented design principles, combined with input validation through
exception handling, further strengthens the program’s stability and reduces the
likelihood of runtime errors. However, the program does not fully meet all
requirements in terms of usability and reliability. For instance, input
handling for time bands and passenger types is strict and case-sensitive, so
entries like “off peak” instead of “OFF_PEAK” result in errors, which can
reduce user-friendliness. Validation for certain inputs, such as zone ranges,
is also limited, and there are minor inconsistencies in output formatting,
particularly regarding decimal precision in fare displays. While these issues
do not compromise the program’s core functionality, they point to areas where
improvements could make the system more user-friendly and better equipped for
real-world applications.

**Strengths of the Program:**

The CityRideLite
program exhibits several key strengths. Its object-oriented design is both
clear and well-structured, with individual classes, such as Journey,
JourneyManager, and FileManager, each assigned with specific responsibilities.
This approach enhances the program’s readability and maintainability. The fare
calculation system stands out for its accuracy and reliability, using
BigDecimal to ensure accurate monetary values and consistently applying
discounts and daily spending caps. The program also offers a comprehensive set
of features, including robust journey management (add, view, search, update,
delete) and data persistence via both JSON and CSV formats, which increases its
usability for real-world use. Furthermore, the implementation of exception
handling contributes to system stability by preventing crashes due to invalid
user input. Overall, these elements combine to create a well-rounded and
reliable system.

**Weaknesses of the Program:**

Despite its strengths,
the program does present some notable weaknesses. The input handling is
relatively inflexible, requiring users to enter data in exact formats such as
“OFF_PEAK,” which can increase the likelihood of input errors and reduce
overall usability. Validation for certain fields, such as zone ranges, is
limited, potentially allowing invalid data to be accepted. While the
console-based interface is operational, it is less user-friendly than a
graphical alternative. There are also minor irregularities in output
formatting, especially regarding decimal precision, and some repetitive
input-handling code that could be simplified to improve efficiency. Overall,
although the program performs well functionally, enhancements in usability,
input validation, and code optimisation would further improve its quality and
user experience.

**Areas for Improvement:**

The program could be
improved in several ways to make it easier to use and more reliable overall.
One of the biggest improvements would be to handle user input more flexibly-for
example, letting users type something like “off peak” and having the system
interpret it correctly instead of requiring them to enter a strict format like
“OFF_PEAK.” Allowing a wider range of acceptable inputs is a common usability
principle and helps prevent user frustration.It would also help to strengthen
validation, such as checking whether zone numbers fall within a valid range,
which improves robustness and reduces errors .Another important
improvement would be switching from simple strings to proper date‑and‑time
types like LocalDateTime. This would make the data easier to format, sort,
and work within future features. The interface could also be made more user‑friendly
by replacing the console layout with a graphical interface, giving users a
clearer and more intuitive way to interact with the system, which aligns with
standard usability recommendations to minimize memory load and make actions
visible .From a coding perspective, reducing repeated logic-especially in
the input‑handling parts-by using helper methods would make the program cleaner
and easier to maintain. On top of that, adding new features like sorting
journeys, filtering them by date or passenger type, or improving the formatting
of outputs (for example, using consistent decimal places) would make the system
feel more polished and more like a real‑world application. These kinds of
enhancements help improve the overall quality, reliability, and user experience
of the software.

# Appendices

**Milestone 1:**

Analysis of the
program specification

---

The program
specification describes the development of an extended transport fare
application that builds on the basic version created in Part 1. The primary
function of the system enables users to monitor their daily trips while
computing their travel expenses and safeguarding their travel records through
an improved authentic system. The system introduces new features such as user
profiles, file storage, and an administrator role, which makes it closer to a
real-world application. The system needs to support two distinct user groups
according to the specification which includes both riders and administrators.
Riders create their profiles which they use to manage their daily travel by
entering new journeys and checking their travel progress. Administrators handle
system configuration which includes managing fares and discounts together with
daily caps and peak time windows. The system requires designers to create
distinct system functions which different user groups need to perform their
tasks. The program needs to achieve data persistence according to the
specification because this functionality enables the system to store and
retrieve information through JSON and CSV file formats. The process prevents
user data and travel records from being lost when the system shuts down. The
system needs to execute precise fare computations through base fare and
discount and daily cap application, which necessitates thorough input data
evaluation.

---

**Purpose of the
Program**

---

The purpose of this
program is to develop a transport application that allows users to track their
journeys and calculate travel fares. Riders can create a profile, store their
data, and view journey summaries, while administrators can manage fares, discounts,
and system settings. The program also uses file handling to save and load data,
making it more practical and realistic for real-world use.

---

**Core program
functionality**

---

The main functions of
the program are system configuration and managing rider journeys. Users can
create, load, and save rider profiles with details such as name, passenger
type, and payment method. Riders are able to add, edit, and delete journeys,
and each journey records information such as zones travelled, time band, and
calculated fare. The system also ensures that all journey data is stored and
updated correctly. The program calculates fares based on zones and whether the
journey is peak or off-peak. It applies discounts based on passenger type and
also applies daily caps to ensure the total cost does not exceed a set limit.
This helps to provide accurate and fair pricing for users. The system also
allows users to view running totals and individual journey costs. In addition,
the system can import and export journey data using CSV files, making it easier
to manage large amounts of data. It also saves and loads data using JSON files
so that user profiles and journeys can be stored between sessions and accessed
later. The system also generates end-of-day summaries, including total cost,
number of journeys, average fare, and other useful information such as the most
expensive journey and savings made from caps. These summaries help users
understand their daily travel spending. An admin role is included, which allows
authorised users to manage fare rules, discounts, daily caps, and peak time
settings. The system ensures that all changes made by the admin are validated
before being saved, helping to maintain accuracy and consistency across the
program.

---

**System Constraints**

---

The system development
process must consider several constraints. The program requires full user input
validation because invalid zone numbers, empty values, incorrect date or time
formats, and invalid journey IDs can cause errors. The system must show clear
and understandable error messages when incorrect data is entered and must
prevent invalid data from being saved. Another important constraint is file
handling. The program must correctly read and write JSON files for profiles and
configuration data, and CSV files for journeys and reports. The system must
also handle situations such as missing files, incorrect file formats, and file
access errors, while maintaining the accuracy and security of the data.
Security is also a key constraint because only users with a password-protected
login can access admin features. This prevents regular riders from changing
fares, discounts, daily caps, and peak time settings. The program must also
validate all configuration changes before saving to avoid incorrect values affecting
the system. In addition, the program must follow object-oriented programming
principles such as encapsulation, inheritance, and proper class structure. The
system should be organised using methods and classes to improve readability,
testing, and maintenance. As the system is a console-based Java application, it
may be less user-friendly compared to graphical applications. Finally, the
program must follow the dataset and assignment rules, which define fare
calculations, discounts, daily caps, and peak time windows. The system cannot
use values outside the allowed range and must remain consistent with the given
specifications.

---

**Input Process
Output Table**

---

| **Function**         | **Input**                                       | **Process**                                                          | **Output**                       |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Create Rider Profile | Name, passenger<br> type, payment method        | Validate input (no<br> empty values), create object, store in system | Rider profile<br> created        |
| Load Rider Profile   | JSON file                                       | Read file, parse<br> JSON, load into system                          | Profile loaded<br> successfully  |
| Save Rider Profile   | Profile data                                    | Convert object to<br> JSON format and write to file                  | Profile saved                    |
| Add Journey          | Zones, time band,<br> passenger type, date/time | Validate input,<br> calculate zones crossed, compute fare            | Journey added to<br> list        |
| Edit Journey         | Journey ID, updated<br> details                 | Check valid ID,<br> update fields, recalculate fare                  | Journey updated                  |
| Delete Journey       | Journey ID                                      | Validate ID, remove<br> journey, update totals                       | Journey removed                  |

class FileManager {  
private static final ObjectMapper objectMapper = new ObjectMapper()  
.enable(SerializationFeature.INDENT_OUTPUT);

// Save rider profile
to JSON 

public static void
saveProfile(RiderProfile profile, String filePath) { 

    try { 

        objectMapper.writeValue(new
File(filePath), profile); 

        System.out.println("Profile saved
successfully to " + filePath); 

    } catch (IOException e) { 

        System.out.println("Error saving
profile: " + e.getMessage()); 

    } 

} 

// Load rider profile
from JSON 

public static
RiderProfile loadProfile(String filePath) { 

    try { 

        return objectMapper.readValue(new
File(filePath), RiderProfile.class); 

    } catch (IOException e) { 

        System.out.println("Error loading
profile: " + e.getMessage()); 

        return null; 

    } 

} 

// Export journeys to
CSV 

public static void
exportJourneysToCSV(List<Journey> journeys, String filePath) { 

    try (PrintWriter writer = new
PrintWriter(new File(filePath))) { 

        writer.println("StartZone,EndZone,TimeBand,PassengerType,BaseFare,FinalFare"); 

        for (Journey journey : journeys) { 

            writer.printf("%d,%d,%s,%s,%.2f,%.2f%n", 

                    journey.getStartZone(), 

                    journey.getEndZone(), 

                    journey.getTimeBand(), 

                    journey.getPassengerType(), 

                    journey.getBaseFare(), 

                    journey.getFinalFare()); 

        } 

        System.out.println("Journeys
exported successfully to " + filePath); 

    } catch (IOException e) { 

        System.out.println("Error
exporting journeys: " + e.getMessage()); 

    } 

} 

// Import journeys
from CSV 

public static
List<Journey> importJourneysFromCSV(String filePath) { 

    List<Journey> journeys = new
ArrayList<>(); 

    try (BufferedReader reader = new
BufferedReader(new FileReader(filePath))) { 

        String line = reader.readLine(); //
Skip header 

        while ((line = reader.readLine()) !=
null) { 

            String[] parts =
line.split(","); 

            int startZone =
Integer.parseInt(parts[0]); 

            int endZone =
Integer.parseInt(parts[1]); 

            CityRideDataset.TimeBand timeBand =
CityRideDataset.TimeBand.valueOf(parts[2]); 

            CityRideDataset.PassengerType
passengerType = CityRideDataset.PassengerType.valueOf(parts[3]); 

            BigDecimal baseFare = new
BigDecimal(parts[4]); 

            BigDecimal finalFare = new
BigDecimal(parts[5]); 

            journeys.add(new Journey(startZone,
endZone, timeBand, passengerType, baseFare, finalFare)); 

        } 

        System.out.println("Journeys
imported successfully from " + filePath); 

    } catch (IOException e) { 

        System.out.println("Error
importing journeys: " + e.getMessage()); 

    } 

    return journeys; 

} 

}

class JourneyManager {  
private List journeyList;

private
Map<CityRideDataset.PassengerType, BigDecimal> dailySpending; 

public
JourneyManager() { 

    journeyList = new ArrayList<>(); 

    dailySpending = new HashMap<>(); 

    for (CityRideDataset.PassengerType
PassangerType : CityRideDataset.PassengerType.values()) { 

        dailySpending.put(PassangerType,
BigDecimal.ZERO); 

    } 

} 

/** 

 * Calculates final fare by applying passenger
discount then enforcing the     * daily
spending cap. Uses a single result variable to satisfy the NTIC     * single-return guideline.     */ 

public BigDecimal
calculateFare(int fromZone, int toZone, 

                                CityRideDataset.TimeBand timeBand, 

                                CityRideDataset.PassengerType passengerType) { 

    BigDecimal result = null; 

    BigDecimal baseFare =
CityRideDataset.getBaseFare(fromZone, toZone, timeBand); 

    if (baseFare == null) { 

        System.out.println("Error: Invalid
zone combination."); 

    } 

    else { 

        /* Apply percentage discount based on
passenger type */ 

        BigDecimal discountRate =
CityRideDataset.DISCOUNT_RATE.get(passengerType); 

        BigDecimal discountAmount =
baseFare.multiply(discountRate) 

                .setScale(2,
RoundingMode.HALF_UP); 

        BigDecimal discountedFare =
baseFare.subtract(discountAmount) 

                .setScale(2,
RoundingMode.HALF_UP); 

        /* Enforce daily cap so total spend
does not exceed the limit */ 

        BigDecimal currentSpending =
dailySpending.getOrDefault( 

                passengerType,
BigDecimal.ZERO); 

        BigDecimal cap =
CityRideDataset.DAILY_CAP.get(passengerType); 

        BigDecimal remaining =
cap.subtract(currentSpending); 

        if
(remaining.compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) <= 0) { 

            System.out.println("Daily cap
reached for " + passengerType 

                    + ". This journey is
free!"); 

            result = BigDecimal.ZERO; 

        } else if
(discountedFare.compareTo(remaining) > 0) { 

            System.out.println("Fare
capped to remaining daily allowance: £" 

                    + remaining); 

            result = remaining; 

        } else { 

            result = discountedFare; 

        } 

    } 

    return result; 

} 

/* Delegates to the
dataset to retrieve the base fare for a zone pair */ 

public BigDecimal
getBaseFare(int fromZone, int toZone, CityRideDataset.TimeBand timeBand) { 

    return
CityRideDataset.getBaseFare(fromZone, toZone, timeBand); 

} 

/* Records a new
journey and updates the daily spending tracker */ 

public void
addJourney(Journey j) { 

    journeyList.add(j); 

    BigDecimal currentSpending =
dailySpending.getOrDefault(j.getPassengerType(), BigDecimal.ZERO); 

    dailySpending.put(j.getPassengerType(),
currentSpending.add(j.getFinalFare())); 

    System.out.println("Journey added
successfully."); 

} 

/* Lists every
recorded journey, or a message if the list is empty */ 

public void
showAllJourneys() { 

    if (journeyList.isEmpty()) { 

        System.out.println("No journeys
recorded yet."); 

    } else { 

        for (int i = 0; i <
journeyList.size(); i++) { 

            System.out.print((i + 1) + ".
"); 

            journeyList.get(i).displayJourney(); 

        } 

    } 

} 

/* Returns the first
journey matching both zones, or null if not found */ 

public Journey
searchJourney(int startZone, int endZone) { 

    Journey result = null; 

    for (Journey current : journeyList) { 

        if (current.getStartZone() ==
startZone 

                && current.getEndZone()
== endZone) { 

            result = current; 

            break; // stop at first match 

        } 

    } 

    return result; 

} 

/* Removes a journey
by list index and reverses its spending impact */ 

public void
deleteJourney(int index) { 

    if (index >= 0 && index <
journeyList.size()) { 

        Journey removed =
journeyList.remove(index); 

        BigDecimal currentSpending =
dailySpending.get(removed.getPassengerType()); 

        dailySpending.put(removed.getPassengerType(),
currentSpending.subtract(removed.getFinalFare())); 

        System.out.println("Journey
deleted successfully."); 

    } else { 

        System.out.println("Invalid
journey number."); 

    } 

} 

/* 

 * Replaces an existing journey's details with
new values.     * Old fare is subtracted
before the new fare is added so the cap     * remains accurate across updates.     */    public void
updateJourney(int index, int newStart, int newEnd, 

                          CityRideDataset.TimeBand newTimeBand, 

                          CityRideDataset.PassengerType newPassengerType) { 

    if (index >= 0 && index <
journeyList.size()) { 

        Journey j =
journeyList.get(index); 

        /* Remove old fare from spending before
recalculating */ 

        BigDecimal oldSpending =
dailySpending.get(j.getPassengerType()); 

        dailySpending.put(j.getPassengerType(),
oldSpending.subtract(j.getFinalFare())); 

        BigDecimal baseFare =
CityRideDataset.getBaseFare(newStart, newEnd, newTimeBand); 

        BigDecimal finalFare =
calculateFare(newStart, newEnd, newTimeBand, newPassengerType); 

        if (finalFare != null &&
baseFare != null) { 

            j.setStartZone(newStart); 

            j.setEndZone(newEnd); 

            j.setTimeBand(newTimeBand); 

            j.setPassengerType(newPassengerType); 

            j.setBaseFare(baseFare); 

            j.setFinalFare(finalFare); 

            BigDecimal newSpending =
dailySpending.getOrDefault(newPassengerType, BigDecimal.ZERO); 

            dailySpending.put(newPassengerType,
newSpending.add(finalFare)); 

            System.out.println("Journey
updated successfully."); 

        } 

    } else { 

        System.out.println("Invalid
journey number."); 

    } 

} 

/* Prints each
passenger type's total spend alongside its daily cap */ 

public void
showDailySpending() { 

    System.out.println("\n--- Daily
Spending Summary ---"); 

    for (CityRideDataset.PassengerType pt :
CityRideDataset.PassengerType.values()) { 

        BigDecimal spent =
dailySpending.getOrDefault(pt, BigDecimal.ZERO); 

        BigDecimal cap =
CityRideDataset.DAILY_CAP.get(pt); 

        System.out.println(pt + ": £"

+ spent + " / £" + cap + " (daily cap)"); 

    } 

} 

}

        int choice; 

        do { 

            System.out.println("\n=====
Admin Menu ====="); 

            System.out.println("1. View
Configuration"); 

            System.out.println("2. Update
Configuration"); 

            System.out.println("3. Exit
Admin Menu"); 

            System.out.print("Choice:
"); 

            choice = scanner.nextInt(); 

            scanner.nextLine(); 

            switch (choice) { 

                case 1:
adminManager.viewConfig(); break; 

                case 2:
adminManager.updateConfig(); break; 

                case 3:
System.out.println("Exiting Admin Menu."); break; 

                default:
System.out.println("Invalid choice. Try again."); 

            } 

        } while (choice != 3); 

    } else { 

        System.out.println("Invalid
password. Access denied."); 

    } 

} 

public void run()
{ 

    int choice; 

    do { 

        System.out.println("\n=====
CityRideLite Menu ====="); 

        System.out.println("1. Add
Journey"); 

        System.out.println("2. List
Journeys"); 

        System.out.println("3. Search
Journey"); 

        System.out.println("4. Update
Journey"); 

        System.out.println("5. Delete
Journey"); 

        System.out.println("6. Calculate
Fare"); 

        System.out.println("7. View Daily
Spending"); 

        System.out.println("8. Admin
Menu"); 

        System.out.println("9.
Exit"); 

        System.out.print("Choice:
"); 

        choice = scanner.nextInt(); 

        scanner.nextLine(); 

        switch (choice) { 

            case 1: handleAddJourney();
break; 

            case 2:
journeyManager.showAllJourneys(); break; 

            case 3: handleSearchJourney();
break; 

            case 4: handleUpdateJourney();
break; 

            case 5: handleDeleteJourney();
break; 

            case 6: handleCalculateFare();
break; 

            case 7:
journeyManager.showDailySpending(); break; 

            case 8: handleAdminMenu();
break; 

            case 9:
System.out.println("Exiting CityRideLite. Goodbye!"); break; 

            default:
System.out.println("Invalid choice. Try again."); 

        } 

    } while (choice != 9); 

} 

public static void
main(String[] args) { 

    CityRideLite app = new CityRideLite(); 

    app.run(); 

}

# Introduction:

The CityRideLite project is a console‑based
Java application designed to simulate a simplified public transport fare
system. Its main purpose is to let users manage and track their journeys while
applying rules such as zone‑based pricing, discounts, and daily fare caps. The
program allows users to add, view, search, update, and delete journeys, with
fares calculated automatically based on zones travelled, time band (peak or off‑peak),
and passenger type, including adults, students, children, and senior citizens.
It also keeps track of daily spending and applies the correct cap for each
passenger category. To ensure data persistence, the application supports saving
and loading journeys in JSON format, as well as importing and exporting records
through CSV files. An admin menu with password protection is included for
configuration management. Overall, the system demonstrates solid use of object‑oriented
programming, file handling, input validation, and structured program design.  

# Analysis:

**Analysis of the program specification**

The main requirements
of the system aim to transform the basic fare calculator into a more complete
and realistic transport management application. To accomplish this, the system
must support two user roles-riders and administrators-each with distinct
responsibilities, ensuring that the paragraph maintains a clear, unified focus
as recommended in guidance about keeping one main idea per paragraph. Riders
should be able to create profiles, record their journeys, and monitor daily travel
and spending, while administrators need tools to configure fares, discounts,
daily caps, and peak/off‑peak time settings. The system must also provide full
journey management, including adding, viewing, searching, updating, and
deleting records, with accurate fare calculations based on zones, time bands,
and passenger types, and the correct application of discounts and daily caps.
Maintaining coherence within the paragraph aligns with guidance that readers
rely on early sentences to understand direction and purpose . Additionally,
data persistence is required through JSON saving/loading and CSV import/export
to prevent data loss. Robust input validation and error handling must be
included to maintain reliability, and the system should follow object‑oriented
principles by organising functionality into separate classes, supporting
clarity and structure within the system- similar to how strong paragraphs
maintain organised and relevant development.

| Updated journey inputs    | Recalculate fare and update record            | “Journey updated successfully”            |

# Evaluation:

**Effectiveness of the program:**

The CityRideLite program successfully meets
its primary requirements by applying all key functionalities expected of the
system. Users can manage journeys efficiently through features that allow
adding, viewing, searching, updating, and deleting records, thereby it fully
meets the main goal of journey management. The fare calculation component
functions as designed, accurately accounting for zones, time bands, and
passenger categories, and applying appropriate discounts while applying the
daily spending cap. This demonstrates that the system processes fares both
reliably and accurately. The program further meets the requirement to ensure
data retention by allowing users to save and load data in JSON format and to
import or export records using CSV files, making it easy to store and reuse
information whenever needed. Input validation, achieved through exception
handling, enhances the program’s stability by reducing the risk of errors or
system crashes caused by invalid user input.Taken together, these features show
that the program not only fulfils all specified requirements but also provides
a durable and dependable user experience.

**If the program meet all the requirements?** **If not, why not?**

The CityRideLite program meets most of the
key requirements set out in the brief and is effective in delivering the core
functionalities of the system. It provides a durable journey and management
features, including adding, viewing, searching, updating, and deleting
journeys, which form the core of the application. The fare calculation logic is
accurately implemented, taking into account zones, time bands, and passenger
types, and correctly applies discounts and daily spending caps to ensure
reliable results. The program also satisfies the data persistence requirement
through JSON save/load and CSV export/import capabilities. The application of
object-oriented design principles, combined with input validation through
exception handling, further strengthens the program’s stability and reduces the
likelihood of runtime errors. However, the program does not fully meet all
requirements in terms of usability and reliability. For instance, input
handling for time bands and passenger types is strict and case-sensitive, so
entries like “off peak” instead of “OFF_PEAK” result in errors, which can
reduce user-friendliness. Validation for certain inputs, such as zone ranges,
is also limited, and there are minor inconsistencies in output formatting,
particularly regarding decimal precision in fare displays. While these issues
do not compromise the program’s core functionality, they point to areas where
improvements could make the system more user-friendly and better equipped for
real-world applications.

**Strengths of the Program:**

The CityRideLite
program exhibits several key strengths. Its object-oriented design is both
clear and well-structured, with individual classes, such as Journey,
JourneyManager, and FileManager, each assigned with specific responsibilities.
This approach enhances the program’s readability and maintainability. The fare
calculation system stands out for its accuracy and reliability, using
BigDecimal to ensure accurate monetary values and consistently applying
discounts and daily spending caps. The program also offers a comprehensive set
of features, including robust journey management (add, view, search, update,
delete) and data persistence via both JSON and CSV formats, which increases its
usability for real-world use. Furthermore, the implementation of exception
handling contributes to system stability by preventing crashes due to invalid
user input. Overall, these elements combine to create a well-rounded and
reliable system.

**Weaknesses of the Program:**

Despite its strengths,
the program does present some notable weaknesses. The input handling is
relatively inflexible, requiring users to enter data in exact formats such as
“OFF_PEAK,” which can increase the likelihood of input errors and reduce
overall usability. Validation for certain fields, such as zone ranges, is
limited, potentially allowing invalid data to be accepted. While the
console-based interface is operational, it is less user-friendly than a
graphical alternative. There are also minor irregularities in output
formatting, especially regarding decimal precision, and some repetitive
input-handling code that could be simplified to improve efficiency. Overall,
although the program performs well functionally, enhancements in usability,
input validation, and code optimisation would further improve its quality and
user experience.

**Areas for Improvement:**

The program could be
improved in several ways to make it easier to use and more reliable overall.
One of the biggest improvements would be to handle user input more flexibly-for
example, letting users type something like “off peak” and having the system
interpret it correctly instead of requiring them to enter a strict format like
“OFF_PEAK.” Allowing a wider range of acceptable inputs is a common usability
principle and helps prevent user frustration.It would also help to strengthen
validation, such as checking whether zone numbers fall within a valid range,
which improves robustness and reduces errors .Another important
improvement would be switching from simple strings to proper date‑and‑time
types like LocalDateTime. This would make the data easier to format, sort,
and work within future features. The interface could also be made more user‑friendly
by replacing the console layout with a graphical interface, giving users a
clearer and more intuitive way to interact with the system, which aligns with
standard usability recommendations to minimize memory load and make actions
visible .From a coding perspective, reducing repeated logic-especially in
the input‑handling parts-by using helper methods would make the program cleaner
and easier to maintain. On top of that, adding new features like sorting
journeys, filtering them by date or passenger type, or improving the formatting
of outputs (for example, using consistent decimal places) would make the system
feel more polished and more like a real‑world application. These kinds of
enhancements help improve the overall quality, reliability, and user experience
of the software.

# Appendices

**Milestone 1:**

Analysis of the
program specification

---

The program
specification describes the development of an extended transport fare
application that builds on the basic version created in Part 1. The primary
function of the system enables users to monitor their daily trips while
computing their travel expenses and safeguarding their travel records through
an improved authentic system. The system introduces new features such as user
profiles, file storage, and an administrator role, which makes it closer to a
real-world application. The system needs to support two distinct user groups
according to the specification which includes both riders and administrators.
Riders create their profiles which they use to manage their daily travel by
entering new journeys and checking their travel progress. Administrators handle
system configuration which includes managing fares and discounts together with
daily caps and peak time windows. The system requires designers to create
distinct system functions which different user groups need to perform their
tasks. The program needs to achieve data persistence according to the
specification because this functionality enables the system to store and
retrieve information through JSON and CSV file formats. The process prevents
user data and travel records from being lost when the system shuts down. The
system needs to execute precise fare computations through base fare and
discount and daily cap application, which necessitates thorough input data
evaluation.

---

**Purpose of the
Program**

---

The purpose of this
program is to develop a transport application that allows users to track their
journeys and calculate travel fares. Riders can create a profile, store their
data, and view journey summaries, while administrators can manage fares, discounts,
and system settings. The program also uses file handling to save and load data,
making it more practical and realistic for real-world use.

---

**Core program
functionality**

---

The main functions of
the program are system configuration and managing rider journeys. Users can
create, load, and save rider profiles with details such as name, passenger
type, and payment method. Riders are able to add, edit, and delete journeys,
and each journey records information such as zones travelled, time band, and
calculated fare. The system also ensures that all journey data is stored and
updated correctly. The program calculates fares based on zones and whether the
journey is peak or off-peak. It applies discounts based on passenger type and
also applies daily caps to ensure the total cost does not exceed a set limit.
This helps to provide accurate and fair pricing for users. The system also
allows users to view running totals and individual journey costs. In addition,
the system can import and export journey data using CSV files, making it easier
to manage large amounts of data. It also saves and loads data using JSON files
so that user profiles and journeys can be stored between sessions and accessed
later. The system also generates end-of-day summaries, including total cost,
number of journeys, average fare, and other useful information such as the most
expensive journey and savings made from caps. These summaries help users
understand their daily travel spending. An admin role is included, which allows
authorised users to manage fare rules, discounts, daily caps, and peak time
settings. The system ensures that all changes made by the admin are validated
before being saved, helping to maintain accuracy and consistency across the
program.

---

**System Constraints**

---

The system development
process must consider several constraints. The program requires full user input
validation because invalid zone numbers, empty values, incorrect date or time
formats, and invalid journey IDs can cause errors. The system must show clear
and understandable error messages when incorrect data is entered and must
prevent invalid data from being saved. Another important constraint is file
handling. The program must correctly read and write JSON files for profiles and
configuration data, and CSV files for journeys and reports. The system must
also handle situations such as missing files, incorrect file formats, and file
access errors, while maintaining the accuracy and security of the data.
Security is also a key constraint because only users with a password-protected
login can access admin features. This prevents regular riders from changing
fares, discounts, daily caps, and peak time settings. The program must also
validate all configuration changes before saving to avoid incorrect values affecting
the system. In addition, the program must follow object-oriented programming
principles such as encapsulation, inheritance, and proper class structure. The
system should be organised using methods and classes to improve readability,
testing, and maintenance. As the system is a console-based Java application, it
may be less user-friendly compared to graphical applications. Finally, the
program must follow the dataset and assignment rules, which define fare
calculations, discounts, daily caps, and peak time windows. The system cannot
use values outside the allowed range and must remain consistent with the given
specifications.

final class
CityRideDataset {

private
CityRideDataset() {} 

public static final
int MIN_ZONE = 1; 

public static final
int MAX_ZONE = 5; 

public enum TimeBand
{ 

    PEAK, 

    OFF_PEAK 

} 

public enum
PassengerType { 

    ADULT, 

    STUDENT, 

    CHILD, 

    SENIOR_CITIZEN 

} 

public static final
Map<PassengerType, BigDecimal> DISCOUNT_RATE = Map.of( 

        PassengerType.ADULT, new
BigDecimal("0.00"), 

        PassengerType.STUDENT, new
BigDecimal("0.25"), 

        PassengerType.CHILD, new
BigDecimal("0.50"), 

        PassengerType.SENIOR_CITIZEN, new
BigDecimal("0.30") 

); 

public static final
Map<PassengerType, BigDecimal> DAILY_CAP = Map.of( 

        PassengerType.ADULT, new
BigDecimal("8.00"), 

        PassengerType.STUDENT, new
BigDecimal("6.00"), 

        PassengerType.CHILD, new
BigDecimal("4.00"), 

        PassengerType.SENIOR_CITIZEN, new
BigDecimal("7.00") 

); 

public static final
Map<String, BigDecimal> BASE_FARE = buildBaseFare(); 

public static
BigDecimal getBaseFare(int fromZone, int toZone, TimeBand timeBand) { 

    return BASE_FARE.get(key(fromZone, toZone,
timeBand)); 

} 

public static String
key(int fromZone, int toZone, TimeBand timeBand) { 

    return fromZone + "-" + toZone +
"-" + timeBand.name(); 

} 

private static
BigDecimal money(String amount) { 

    return new BigDecimal(amount).setScale(2,
RoundingMode.HALF_UP); 

}

Map<String, BigDecimal> buildBaseFare() {

put(m,1,4,TimeBand.PEAK,"4.40"); 

    put(m,1,5,TimeBand.PEAK,"5.00"); 

    put(m,2,1,TimeBand.PEAK,"3.20");
put(m,2,2,TimeBand.PEAK,"2.30"); 

    put(m,2,3,TimeBand.PEAK,"3.10");
put(m,2,4,TimeBand.PEAK,"3.80");

    put(m,3,1,TimeBand.PEAK,"3.80");
put(m,3,2,TimeBand.PEAK,"3.10");

put(m,3,4,TimeBand.PEAK,"3.00");

class FileManager {  
private static final ObjectMapper objectMapper = new ObjectMapper()  
.enable(SerializationFeature.INDENT_OUTPUT);

// Save rider profile
to JSON 

public static void
saveProfile(RiderProfile profile, String filePath) { 

    try { 

        objectMapper.writeValue(new
File(filePath), profile); 

        System.out.println("Profile saved
successfully to " + filePath); 

    } catch (IOException e) { 

        System.out.println("Error saving
profile: " + e.getMessage()); 

    } 

} 

// Load rider profile
from JSON 

public static
RiderProfile loadProfile(String filePath) { 

    try { 

        return objectMapper.readValue(new
File(filePath), RiderProfile.class); 

    } catch (IOException e) { 

        System.out.println("Error loading
profile: " + e.getMessage()); 

        return null; 

    } 

} 

// Export journeys to
CSV 

public static void
exportJourneysToCSV(List<Journey> journeys, String filePath) { 

    try (PrintWriter writer = new
PrintWriter(new File(filePath))) { 

        writer.println("StartZone,EndZone,TimeBand,PassengerType,BaseFare,FinalFare"); 

        for (Journey journey : journeys) { 

            writer.printf("%d,%d,%s,%s,%.2f,%.2f%n", 

                    journey.getStartZone(), 

                    journey.getEndZone(), 

                    journey.getTimeBand(), 

                    journey.getPassengerType(), 

                    journey.getBaseFare(), 

                    journey.getFinalFare()); 

        } 

        System.out.println("Journeys
exported successfully to " + filePath); 

    } catch (IOException e) { 

        System.out.println("Error
exporting journeys: " + e.getMessage()); 

    } 

} 

// Import journeys
from CSV 

public static
List<Journey> importJourneysFromCSV(String filePath) { 

    List<Journey> journeys = new
ArrayList<>(); 

    try (BufferedReader reader = new
BufferedReader(new FileReader(filePath))) { 

        String line = reader.readLine(); //
Skip header 

        while ((line = reader.readLine()) !=
null) { 

            String[] parts =
line.split(","); 

            int startZone =
Integer.parseInt(parts[0]); 

            int endZone =
Integer.parseInt(parts[1]); 

            CityRideDataset.TimeBand timeBand =
CityRideDataset.TimeBand.valueOf(parts[2]); 

            CityRideDataset.PassengerType
passengerType = CityRideDataset.PassengerType.valueOf(parts[3]); 

            BigDecimal baseFare = new
BigDecimal(parts[4]); 

            BigDecimal finalFare = new
BigDecimal(parts[5]); 

            journeys.add(new Journey(startZone,
endZone, timeBand, passengerType, baseFare, finalFare)); 

        } 

        System.out.println("Journeys
imported successfully from " + filePath); 

    } catch (IOException e) { 

        System.out.println("Error
importing journeys: " + e.getMessage()); 

    } 

    return journeys; 

} 

}

class JourneyManager {  
private List journeyList;

private
Map<CityRideDataset.PassengerType, BigDecimal> dailySpending; 

public
JourneyManager() { 

    journeyList = new ArrayList<>(); 

    dailySpending = new HashMap<>(); 

    for (CityRideDataset.PassengerType
PassangerType : CityRideDataset.PassengerType.values()) { 

        dailySpending.put(PassangerType,
BigDecimal.ZERO); 

    } 

} 

/** 

 * Calculates final fare by applying passenger
discount then enforcing the     * daily
spending cap. Uses a single result variable to satisfy the NTIC     * single-return guideline.     */ 

public BigDecimal
calculateFare(int fromZone, int toZone, 

                                CityRideDataset.TimeBand timeBand, 

                                CityRideDataset.PassengerType passengerType) { 

    BigDecimal result = null; 

    BigDecimal baseFare =
CityRideDataset.getBaseFare(fromZone, toZone, timeBand); 

    if (baseFare == null) { 

        System.out.println("Error: Invalid
zone combination."); 

    } 

    else { 

        /* Apply percentage discount based on
passenger type */ 

        BigDecimal discountRate =
CityRideDataset.DISCOUNT_RATE.get(passengerType); 

        BigDecimal discountAmount =
baseFare.multiply(discountRate) 

                .setScale(2,
RoundingMode.HALF_UP); 

        BigDecimal discountedFare =
baseFare.subtract(discountAmount) 

                .setScale(2,
RoundingMode.HALF_UP); 

        /* Enforce daily cap so total spend
does not exceed the limit */ 

        BigDecimal currentSpending =
dailySpending.getOrDefault( 

                passengerType,
BigDecimal.ZERO); 

        BigDecimal cap =
CityRideDataset.DAILY_CAP.get(passengerType); 

        BigDecimal remaining =
cap.subtract(currentSpending); 

        if
(remaining.compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) <= 0) { 

            System.out.println("Daily cap
reached for " + passengerType 

                    + ". This journey is
free!"); 

            result = BigDecimal.ZERO; 

        } else if
(discountedFare.compareTo(remaining) > 0) { 

            System.out.println("Fare
capped to remaining daily allowance: £" 

                    + remaining); 

            result = remaining; 

        } else { 

            result = discountedFare; 

        } 

    } 

    return result; 

} 

/* Delegates to the
dataset to retrieve the base fare for a zone pair */ 

public BigDecimal
getBaseFare(int fromZone, int toZone, CityRideDataset.TimeBand timeBand) { 

    return
CityRideDataset.getBaseFare(fromZone, toZone, timeBand); 

} 

/* Records a new
journey and updates the daily spending tracker */ 

public void
addJourney(Journey j) { 

    journeyList.add(j); 

    BigDecimal currentSpending =
dailySpending.getOrDefault(j.getPassengerType(), BigDecimal.ZERO); 

    dailySpending.put(j.getPassengerType(),
currentSpending.add(j.getFinalFare())); 

    System.out.println("Journey added
successfully."); 

} 

/* Lists every
recorded journey, or a message if the list is empty */ 

public void
showAllJourneys() { 

    if (journeyList.isEmpty()) { 

        System.out.println("No journeys
recorded yet."); 

    } else { 

        for (int i = 0; i <
journeyList.size(); i++) { 

            System.out.print((i + 1) + ".
"); 

            journeyList.get(i).displayJourney(); 

        } 

    } 

} 

/* Returns the first
journey matching both zones, or null if not found */ 

public Journey
searchJourney(int startZone, int endZone) { 

    Journey result = null; 

    for (Journey current : journeyList) { 

        if (current.getStartZone() ==
startZone 

                && current.getEndZone()
== endZone) { 

            result = current; 

            break; // stop at first match 

        } 

    } 

    return result; 

} 

/* Removes a journey
by list index and reverses its spending impact */ 

public void
deleteJourney(int index) { 

    if (index >= 0 && index <
journeyList.size()) { 

        Journey removed =
journeyList.remove(index); 

        BigDecimal currentSpending =
dailySpending.get(removed.getPassengerType()); 

        dailySpending.put(removed.getPassengerType(),
currentSpending.subtract(removed.getFinalFare())); 

        System.out.println("Journey
deleted successfully."); 

    } else { 

        System.out.println("Invalid
journey number."); 

    } 

} 

/* 

 * Replaces an existing journey's details with
new values.     * Old fare is subtracted
before the new fare is added so the cap     * remains accurate across updates.     */    public void
updateJourney(int index, int newStart, int newEnd, 

                          CityRideDataset.TimeBand newTimeBand, 

                          CityRideDataset.PassengerType newPassengerType) { 

    if (index >= 0 && index <
journeyList.size()) { 

        Journey j =
journeyList.get(index); 

        /* Remove old fare from spending before
recalculating */ 

        BigDecimal oldSpending =
dailySpending.get(j.getPassengerType()); 

        dailySpending.put(j.getPassengerType(),
oldSpending.subtract(j.getFinalFare())); 

        BigDecimal baseFare =
CityRideDataset.getBaseFare(newStart, newEnd, newTimeBand); 

        BigDecimal finalFare =
calculateFare(newStart, newEnd, newTimeBand, newPassengerType); 

        if (finalFare != null &&
baseFare != null) { 

            j.setStartZone(newStart); 

            j.setEndZone(newEnd); 

            j.setTimeBand(newTimeBand); 

            j.setPassengerType(newPassengerType); 

            j.setBaseFare(baseFare); 

            j.setFinalFare(finalFare); 

            BigDecimal newSpending =
dailySpending.getOrDefault(newPassengerType, BigDecimal.ZERO); 

            dailySpending.put(newPassengerType,
newSpending.add(finalFare)); 

            System.out.println("Journey
updated successfully."); 

        } 

    } else { 

        System.out.println("Invalid
journey number."); 

    } 

} 

/* Prints each
passenger type's total spend alongside its daily cap */ 

public void
showDailySpending() { 

    System.out.println("\n--- Daily
Spending Summary ---"); 

    for (CityRideDataset.PassengerType pt :
CityRideDataset.PassengerType.values()) { 

        BigDecimal spent =
dailySpending.getOrDefault(pt, BigDecimal.ZERO); 

        BigDecimal cap =
CityRideDataset.DAILY_CAP.get(pt); 

        System.out.println(pt + ": £"

+ spent + " / £" + cap + " (daily cap)"); 

    } 

} 

}  
public class CityRideLite {  
private Scanner scanner;  
private JourneyManager journeyManager;  
private RiderProfile riderProfile;

public CityRideLite()
{ 

    scanner = new Scanner(System.in); 

    journeyManager = new JourneyManager(); 

} 

private void
handleAdminMenu() { 

    AdminManager adminManager = new
AdminManager(); 

    System.out.print("Enter admin
password: "); 

    String password = scanner.nextLine(); 

    if (adminManager.authenticate(password))
{ 

        int choice; 

        do { 

            System.out.println("\n=====
Admin Menu ====="); 

            System.out.println("1. View
Configuration"); 

            System.out.println("2. Update
Configuration"); 

            System.out.println("3. Exit
Admin Menu"); 

            System.out.print("Choice:
"); 

            choice = scanner.nextInt(); 

            scanner.nextLine(); 

            switch (choice) { 

                case 1:
adminManager.viewConfig(); break; 

                case 2:
adminManager.updateConfig(); break; 

                case 3:
System.out.println("Exiting Admin Menu."); break; 

                default:
System.out.println("Invalid choice. Try again."); 

            } 

        } while (choice != 3); 

    } else { 

        System.out.println("Invalid
password. Access denied."); 

    } 

} 

public void run()
{ 

    int choice; 

    do { 

        System.out.println("\n=====
CityRideLite Menu ====="); 

        System.out.println("1. Add
Journey"); 

        System.out.println("2. List
Journeys"); 

        System.out.println("3. Search
Journey"); 

        System.out.println("4. Update
Journey"); 

        System.out.println("5. Delete
Journey"); 

        System.out.println("6. Calculate
Fare"); 

        System.out.println("7. View Daily
Spending"); 

        System.out.println("8. Admin
Menu"); 

        System.out.println("9.
Exit"); 

        System.out.print("Choice:
"); 

        choice = scanner.nextInt(); 

        scanner.nextLine(); 

        switch (choice) { 

            case 1: handleAddJourney();
break; 

            case 2:
journeyManager.showAllJourneys(); break; 

            case 3: handleSearchJourney();
break; 

            case 4: handleUpdateJourney();
break; 

            case 5: handleDeleteJourney();
break; 

            case 6: handleCalculateFare();
break; 

            case 7:
journeyManager.showDailySpending(); break; 

            case 8: handleAdminMenu();
break; 

            case 9:
System.out.println("Exiting CityRideLite. Goodbye!"); break; 

            default:
System.out.println("Invalid choice. Try again."); 

        } 

    } while (choice != 9); 

} 

public static void
main(String[] args) { 

    CityRideLite app = new CityRideLite(); 

    app.run(); 

} 

}
